certificate-errors-desktop.message: Sites with certificate problems show the engine's warning page, with its option to proceed, instead of a dead-end error.

experimental-update-channel.message: Builds from the experimental branch update through their own Experimental channel, shown in Settings only on those builds.

webkit-before-unload.message: On the WebKit browser, a page with unsaved changes asks before its tab closes.

webkit-peek-keeps-referrer.message: Peek opened from a modified link on the WebKit browser keeps the link's referrer.

webkit-pip-residency.message: Report WebKit picture-in-picture state to page residency so a page in picture-in-picture is never unloaded.

experimental-chromium-release.message: Publish experimental releases with the Chromium build as the default download and a WebKit build as an alternate, each on its own update feed, from a prebuilt engine published per engine revision.

now-playing-desktop.message: Now Playing in the desktop browser shows what a tab is playing and can play, pause, skip and mute it.

selection-search-desktop.message: Right-click selected text in the desktop browser to search for it with your Space's search engine.

site-permissions-desktop.message: In the desktop browser, camera, microphone, location and notification requests use Crest's own prompt, are remembered per Space, and can be reviewed and revoked in Site Controls and Privacy.

core-downloads-aggregate.message: Move the download ledger, progress estimation, automatic-download throttle and download risk rules into the portable core so both engines and platforms share them.

theme-accents-desktop.message: Tab icons in the desktop browser take on a site's theme colour, and refreshing a site's icon works there too.

viewport-fit-desktop.message: Split cards and Peek in the desktop browser zoom pages with a fixed minimum width to fit, as they do on WebKit.

clear-site-data-desktop.message: Clear Site Data and Reload works in the desktop browser.

side-panel-quick-window-notice.message: An extension side panel requested from a Quick Window now explains that side panels open in the main window.

extension-side-panel-api-open.message: Extensions that open their side panel themselves, such as ChatGPT, now open it on the first click in the desktop browser.

core-credentials-aggregate.message: Move credential capture, fill, save-plan and recency rules and passkey policies into the portable core, keeping passwords out of it.

core-search-aggregate.message: Move the search engine catalog, search URL construction, custom search engine edits and automatic translation rules into the portable core.

companion-apps-connect.message: Extensions that work with a companion app, such as ChatGPT, 1Password and Claude, now connect to it in the desktop browser even when the app was only set up for Chrome.

core-site-permissions.message: Move site permission decisions, external link and scheme consent, blocked popup notices and sign-in challenge rules into the portable core.

core-link-routing.message: Move link routing, Quick Window retargeting, page presentation, content-blocking rule selection, branding ranges and borrowed-workspace command routing into the portable core.

core-window-state.message: Move window selection repair, split layout capture, tear-off eligibility, manual setup plans, onboarding completion and workspace import review into the portable core.

core-shortcuts-launch-media.message: Move keyboard shortcut defaults and conflicts, numbered tab and Space selection, launch isolation and startup behavior, tab insertion and media session arbitration into the portable core.

core-app-preferences.message: Keep startup, translation, spell checking, automatic Picture in Picture, pinned-tab close, saved-tab favicon and Split View focus preferences in the portable core, importing existing settings once.

engine-neutral-page.message: Split the shared page model from the WebKit adapter and give the Chromium composition a host-commands port instead of direct store edits.

typed-engine-capabilities.message: Declare engine capabilities, statuses and implementations as typed values instead of raw strings, keeping the core descriptor unchanged.

shared-native-page-menus.message: Crest's link and Space actions appear first in native page menus while browser and extension actions stay available.

shared-page-dialogs-auth.message: Page dialogs and website sign-in prompts work across both desktop browser engines.

chromium-feature-flags-settings.message: Chromium feature flags open inside Crest Settings.

chromium-automatic-video-pip.message: Playing Chromium videos can enter Picture in Picture when switching tabs, with a window that settles into a screen corner.

core-session-command-cleanup.message: Route remaining tab, icon, page and retention changes through the core and remove the obsolete core-backed build switch.

committed-page-session-updates.message: Keep unfinished page loads from changing saved tabs or history while preserving completed page titles and icons.

engine-owned-site-permissions.message: Permission changes made in Settings or Site Controls now reach open pages without reloading them.

page-security-and-find-counts.message: Site Controls now tell certificate errors, mixed content and dangerous sites apart, and Find in Page shows how many matches a page has where the engine can count them.

core-data-only-selection.message: Keep the viewed Space and tab as window state, remove the Swift session editing surface and its copies of core rules, and route launch cleanup and retention through core commands.

core-typed-policy-requests.message: Decode every core policy request into typed records and keep all rule codes, section names and mode values in their central definitions.

mobile-completed-page-titles.message: Background tabs on iPhone keep the page's real title instead of its site name.

swift-typed-core-boundary.message: Send every core command, policy question and sync operation through typed operation names and Codable models instead of raw strings and dictionaries.

import-opens-first-tab.message: Importing bookmarks or a Crest archive into a new Space opens that Space on its first tab again.

compact-sidebar-hover-sync.message: In compact mode the sidebar opens and closes reliably on hover again.

tab-tear-off-new-window.message: Dragging a tab out of a window opens it in a new window again.

update-whats-new-window.message: What's New on the sidebar's update card opens the full release notes again.

store-first-presentation-state.message: Store window presentation, find, peek and Space lock state before announcing a change, so a render SwiftUI performs during the announcement never keeps a stale value.

typed-core-contract-generator.message: Download intents, changes and rejections are typed C# records, and a generator derives the core codec, Swift models and C header from them.

downloads-typed-core-contract.message: Downloads run through the typed core contract, with one core per process and one download center per browsing mode across windows.

download-progress-risk-queries.message: Download progress and risk are typed core queries instead of JSON policy operations.

core-typed-tab-records.message: The core holds tabs, folders, splits, archive and history as typed records instead of JSON trees, with the stored format unchanged.

core-typed-session-records.message: The core holds Space settings and the session as typed records, and workspace import edits them directly.

credential-typed-queries.message: Credential and passkey decisions are typed core queries, and each app shares one passkey access controller.

search-content-blocking-typed-queries.message: Custom search engine admission and Balanced content-blocking rules are typed core queries.

link-routing-typed-queries.message: External link routing and Quick Window site keys are typed core queries.

generator-fixed-sets.message: The contract generator emits self-describing fixed sets from their C# instances.

download-sets-self-describing.message: Download phases, risk reasons and text fields are self-describing sets whose instances carry their own rules.

download-presentation-on-instances.message: Download phases, risk reasons and row actions carry their own titles and symbols, and a finished download is found by searching Completed.

core-owned-session-file.message: The core opens and saves the session file itself, with the same format and the saves that must reach disk before they return.

swift-stops-saving-session.message: Swift no longer saves the session; the core writes it and reports each save, and quitting waits for the last one.

checkpoint-exports-removed.message: The checkpoint and reservation entry points are removed from the core's C interface.

device-platform-set.message: The device platform is one self-describing set that carries its page-release limits.

shortcut-commands-set.message: Shortcut commands are one set shared by the core and Swift, carrying their sections, default keys, titles and symbols.

settings-navigation-permission-sets.message: Settings destinations, sidebar navigation controls and system permissions describe themselves.

engine-capability-sets.message: Engine capabilities, statuses and adapter roles are typed sets instead of strings.

core-legacy-migration-restore.message: The core carries an installed release's session into its file on first launch and restores the recovery checkpoint itself.

site-permission-sets.message: Site permissions and permission decisions are self-describing sets shared by the core and Swift.

link-sets-self-describing.message: Link route matches, external link destinations and the Peek key describe themselves.

search-provider-set.message: Search providers are one set of built-in and custom engines.

credential-prompt-presentation.message: Credential prompts and passkey status carry their own text and symbols.

pressure-keys-targets-sets.message: Memory pressure levels, shortcut special keys and numbered selection targets share one shape.

core-device-window-store.message: The core keeps each window's shown Space, tabs and split columns in a device store that is saved locally and never synced.

core-decides-window-selection.message: Commands name their window, the core decides what every window shows, and switching tabs and Spaces is faster.

tab-placement-set.message: Tab placements are one set that ranks and describes its sections.

archive-reason-set.message: Archive reasons are spelled once, on the reasons themselves.

tab-icon-mode-set.message: Tab icon modes decide their own inference, favicon use and symbols.

browser-preference-set.message: Each app preference records its own value in the core.

retention-choice-sets.message: Tab cleanup, data retention and Quick Window archive choices carry their own lifetimes and titles.

content-blocking-policy-set.message: Content-blocking policies carry their own rules and titles.

utility-filter-surfaces.message: Utility list filters and surfaces are built from what they show.

policy-answer-sets.message: Link, scheme, download and popup decisions and search-engine flaws describe themselves.

catalog-complete.message: Every user-facing string the apps extract is in the localization catalog.

core-engine-registry-pages.message: The core keeps a registry of engines and knows which page each tab and window hosts.

pages-through-core.message: Every page is opened, moved and released through the core, which refuses pages for locked or deleting Spaces.

engine-names-catalog.message: The engine names are in the localization catalog.

space-settings-apart.message: A Space's settings sit apart from its records in the core, with translation rules and color palettes as records.

session-change-feed.message: The core publishes the session as typed changes, commands no longer carry a revision, and switching tabs is faster.

crest-normalization-core.message: The core keeps a crest's figure and composition the way every device draws them, so Space branding stays steady across sync.

core-sync-staging.message: The core stages sync itself, with each edit's deletion reason and urgency, and saves changes that sync together before returning.

per-record-deletion-reasons.message: Each synced deletion carries the reason of the edit that removed it, so a deleted folder followed by a quick edit still syncs as deleted.

observable-read-model.message: Each workspace, window, Space, tab and folder has its own observable model that updates only when a value changes, and favicons have one store.

history-archive-intents.message: Clearing and removing history, restoring archived tabs and sweeping old records are typed core intents, and the core keeps its own clock.

folder-split-intents.message: Every folder and split-view command is a typed core intent, and a reversed history range is refused instead of doing nothing.

single-page-app-history.message: Pages that change address without reloading, such as a new video or a repository page, now appear in history, and the tab keeps its current address when reopened.

tab-value-intents.message: Renaming a tab, choosing its icon, its saved address and keeping it loaded are typed core intents, and the core publishes each tab's resolved icon, title and saved-address state.

isolated-review-website-data.message: A named isolated review opens its own website data stores, derived from its isolation ID, so a review of a copied session never reads, clears or removes the installed app's cookies and site data.

restored-windows-keep-their-own-content.message: When macOS reopens Crest's windows after you quit, each window comes back on its own Space and tab instead of mirroring the first window.

quit-saves-last-edits.message: A change made right before quitting Crest, or right before it goes to the background on iPhone and iPad, is now always saved and queued for sync.

quit-saves-window-space.message: Switching a window to another Space or resizing a split right before quitting Crest is now always remembered when the window reopens.

tab-lifecycle-intents.message: Opening, closing, copying and moving tabs and keeping Quick Window and Peek pages are typed core intents, and the core decides whether a closed tab archives or goes back.

assistive-app-selectable-text-crash.message: Crest no longer crashes when VoiceOver or another assistive app reads an error page, the About pane or a revealed password.

space-intents.message: Creating, naming, branding, ordering and deleting Spaces are typed core intents, and the core makes each new Space itself.

space-access-intents.message: Locking and unlocking Spaces are typed core intents, and a late unlock result can no longer complete a newer request.

app-preference-intents.message: App preferences, translation rules and launch planning go through typed core intents and queries.

search-engine-intents.message: Adding, editing, choosing and removing search engines are typed core intents, and the chosen engine is stored as a typed value.

static-variables-slice.message: Types made in the Spaces, access, preference and search work keep their static members in their own section.

page-live-state.message: Each page's address, title, loading, history, security and failure live in the core, which also resolves what the person types before a page loads it.

saved-address-return-query.message: The core answers whether a pinned tab can return to its saved address.

page-copies-from-core.message: Copies of a tab, and Quick Window or Peek pages that are kept or archived, start from what the core says the page shows.

forward-after-script-page.message: Forward works again after going back from a page that a site's script opened on its own.

ios-close-policy-test-preferences.message: The iOS saved-tab close test sends its close preference to the test's own core, as the Mac test does.

tab-batch-intents.message: Closing, deleting, copying, filing, splitting, keeping loaded and moving several selected tabs are typed core intents, saved before they return.

tab-move-intents.message: Moving a tab to another Space or window is a typed core intent, and a move between workspaces changes both or neither.

workspace-intents.message: Opening, borrowing and closing workspaces are typed core intents: the core gives each workspace its identity, keeps a temporary window's Space in step with its owner and closes it once the owner stops lending it.

closed-blank-window-stays-closed.message: A closed Blank Window no longer leaves a hidden workspace behind while its window is torn down.

generator-narrowed-unions.message: The contract generator lets a field hold only the intents that derive from one base, so a query can take exactly the intents it answers for.

typed-workspace-import.message: Importing a file, a reviewed browser import or a manual setup runs as typed core intents, and the review screens ask the core what the choices mean.

session-intents-commit-in-lock.message: Session intents commit under the lock that computed them, and refusals without words of their own read as a plain failure.

abi-invalid-session.message: The C ABI program checks a refused seed against the renamed InvalidSession rejection.

import-skips-unchanged-locked-spaces.message: Importing no longer stops at a locked Space the import leaves unchanged.

manual-setup-preview-memo.message: The manual setup previews ask the core again only when the plan or the session changes.

sync-journal-off-launch.message: Crest opens faster with a large sync history.

sync-pauses-on-unreadable-journal.message: Sync pauses and reports an error when this build cannot read the device's sync journal, instead of reading it as empty.

sync-records-fit-client-limits.message: iCloud Sync keeps working when a page has a very long title or address.

tests-seed-sessions-through-intents.message: Tests set up their sessions by seeding a store or sending intents, without the debug session setter.

typed-cloud-sync-intents.message: The core takes cloud sync records through typed intents and refuses a record it cannot take with a named flaw.

cloud-sync-through-core-intents.message: Cloud sync merges, replacements and overwrites run through the core's typed sync intents.

page-reports-without-deferral.message: Page reports apply directly now that only intents reserve the session.

merge-keeps-deletion-reason.message: A folder or history entry you delete just before iCloud Sync brings in changes stays deleted.

sync-transport-typed-queries.message: The cloud transport reads and acknowledges sync uploads through typed core queries, and cloud merges compute off the app's lock.

session-changes-follow-batches.message: Store windows follow every batch of the core's changes that touched their session.

space-cleanup-on-cloud-records.message: Only arriving cloud records restart an unfinished Space cleanup.

sync-merges-off-main-thread.message: Changes from your other devices arrive through iCloud Sync without pausing Crest's windows.

overwrite-keeps-deletion-reason.message: A folder you delete just before choosing this device's copy over iCloud's stays deleted on your other devices.

sync-journal-contracts-in-core.message: The sync journal's contract tests run against the core.

sync-payload-codec-in-core.message: The core reads and writes synced records' payloads.

sync-cloudkit-bytes-in-core.message: The sync transport hands CloudKit the core's own payload bytes.

seed-repair-in-core.message: The core repairs a seeded workspace itself.

sync-json-paths-retired.message: The core owns the sync journal alone; the Swift sync domain and the JSON sync entry points are gone.

sync-json-numbers.message: Synced records read their numbers the same however their JSON was built.

site-permissions-device-store.message: Site permission choices live in the core's device store, carried once from the saved defaults.

shortcuts-device-store.message: Keyboard shortcut choices live in the core's device store, carried once from the saved defaults.

space-permission-reset-revokes.message: Resetting a Space's site permissions always tells its pages to withdraw what they were given.

id-names-plain-uuids.message: Tab, Space, folder, split and window identities are plain UUIDs in Swift, and everything Crest stores keeps the identity spelling earlier builds read.

command-palette-address-morph.message: The command palette now opens out of the address field and closes back into it.

site-origin-one-type.message: Site permissions name a site with the core's origin type everywhere, normalized the same way however the app learns of the site.

read-model-store-first.message: The core's read model stores each change before it tells views about it, so a view that draws during the change shows the new value.

read-model-snapshot-and-view-lint.message: Tests can read a window's session straight from the core's read model, and views may not read a read-model object's whole record.

read-model-sidebar-spike.message: A tab's new favicon redraws only that tab's row, and a debug-only sidebar harness measures what each kind of change redraws.

core-sidebar-outline.message: The core decides what each Space's sidebar lists and publishes only the lists an edit changes, so a new title or address changes no list.

read-model-per-tab-slots.message: Showing another tab tells only the two rows it concerns, and opening or closing a tab tells only the views that looked that tab up.

read-model-sidebar-spike-on-core-outline.message: The debug-only sidebar harness draws the core's published sidebar lists and shown-tab slots, and its checks hold the tighter redraw limits they allow.

space-selector-matching-corners.message: The Space selector's outline and its selection now share the same corners.

session-checks-only-what-an-edit-changed.message: Editing tabs does less work in large sessions.

navigation-publishes-only-changed-rows.message: Navigating in a Space with many tabs or a long history does less work.

space-look-and-accent-from-core.message: The core resolves the branding each Space wears and describes each accent's tint, legacy palette and house look, and generated records carry the core's constants and named values.

tab-order-follows-sidebar.message: Next and previous tab, and ⌘1–⌘9, now follow the order you see in the sidebar.

sidebar-drops-and-selection-queries-in-c.message: The core answers where a sidebar drag may drop, what a sidebar selection holds and which tab Split With Next Tab adds, and decides in one place which edit each drop commits.

sidebar-draws-from-core-read-model.message: The sidebar's sections, folders, splits and pinned tabs draw from the core's published sidebar lists, each row redraws only for its own tab, and every list is lazy.

engine-contract-cpp-codec.message: The engine contract has a generated C++ codec that engines outside Swift can use.

chromium-cpp-binding-reports.message: Chromium reports each page's navigations, state and icon to the core from its own C++ binding.

quick-window-promotion-title.message: A Quick Window page you keep as a tab keeps the page's title instead of its site's name.

sidebar-drags-ask-the-core.message: Dragging in the sidebar now says why a spot won't take what you're holding, a whole split can join the tabs on show or drop into a collapsed folder, and selections stay selectable in long lists.

engine-direct-page-path.message: The platform asks an engine binding for page view work through typed requests and presentations.

chromium-view-work-cpp.message: Chromium answers a page's history, zoom, find, capture and export requests from its own C++ binding.

sidebar-refusals-as-notices.message: When the sidebar can't take a drop, it tells you in the window's notice instead of an alert you have to dismiss.

sidebar-moved-tabs-drag-again.message: Tabs moved together in the sidebar can be dragged again right away.

2026-09-26-close-preparation-core.message: The core prepares closing pages, windows and the app, asking each page whether it may leave

2026-09-26-quick-window-lifetime-applies.message: Changing how long an inactive Quick Window stays open now applies to Quick Windows that are already open

2026-09-26-link-clicks-decided-in-core.message: The core decides what a clicked link does, whether a window a page opens comes to the front and how Quick Windows keep their pages

2026-09-26-drop-into-gone-folder-refused.message: A tab dropped on a folder that was just deleted in another Space now stays where it was instead of landing outside any folder

2026-09-26-ios-download-clear-test.message: The iOS download-clearing test ends its download before clearing it, as the download center now requires

2026-09-26-engine-abi-open-page-transien.message: The engine ABI check sends OpenPage with its new transient presentation field

2026-09-26-site-rules-typed-queries.message: Link, scheme, sign-in, media, location, notification, popup and automatic-download rules are answered by typed core queries

2026-09-26-settings-read-model.message: Settings panes read Spaces and their settings from the core's read model and write edits through the core

2026-09-26-close-quit-through-core.message: Closing tabs and windows or quitting asks pages that want to confirm leaving, and quitting with downloads in progress asks first, in both engines

2026-09-26-cloud-sync-codec-swift62.message: The iOS app builds again with Xcode 26

2026-09-26-launch-stage-drain.message: Storage tests wait for the launch's sync stage instead of stopping at the journal's first announcement

2026-09-26-webkit-crashes-through-core.message: A WebKit page whose content crashes now recovers the same way as Chromium: at once if you're looking at it, or when you next open it

2026-09-26-redirect-test-no-real-load.message: The WebKit redirect test reports its navigation without a real load that could overtake it

2026-09-26-capacity-limits-query.message: The core's capacity limits are answered by a typed query instead of a JSON policy operation

2026-09-26-cloud-transport-state-in-core.message: iCloud sync keeps its progress on this device in Crest's own store, carried over once from the file earlier versions used

2026-09-26-webkit-dialogs-through-core.message: WebKit pages' alert, confirm and prompt dialogs and the leave-page question go through the core, like Chromium's

2026-09-26-webkit-sign-in-through-core.message: WebKit pages' sign-in requests go through the core, offering a saved sign-in first

2026-09-26-capture-permission-rules.message: A camera and microphone request now follows your choice for each device, and blocking a site while it asks refuses the request

2026-09-26-cloud-sync-decisions-in-core.message: Crest decides each step of iCloud sync in its core: starting, pausing for an account change, applying your choice and retrying

2026-09-26-webkit-location-notifications.message: WebKit pages' location and notification requests go through the core, and a page that stops waiting withdraws its question

2026-09-26-system-consent-before-saving.message: Allowing location or notifications for a site is only remembered once macOS or iOS also allows it

2026-09-26-shared-download-prompts.message: Download location and keep-this-file questions are answered in one place for every engine

2026-09-26-window-rules-read-model.message: Browser windows check their Spaces, tabs and folders against the core's published state instead of a copy of the session

2026-09-26-system-consent-all-permission.message: Allowing camera, microphone, location or notifications for a site is only remembered once macOS or iOS also allows it, in both engines

2026-09-26-transient-pages-read-model.message: Quick Windows and Peeks read the Space they browse and the Spaces they offer from the core's published state

2026-09-26-app-scenes-read-model.message: Browser windows check a Space against the core's published state before showing its settings or opening a handed-off link

2026-09-26-core-judges-downloads.message: Crest now checks a download before it's saved, in both engines, and shows its reasons, the site and the Space when it asks; a download blocked by a site's setting can be retried

2026-09-26-import-export-in-core.message: Importing from other browsers and Crest browser-data files, and exporting, now run in Crest's shared core on Mac and iPhone

2026-09-26-manual-setup-in-core.message: The manual setup is held by Crest's shared core, and an unfinished setup on iPhone and iPad waits for the next launch

2026-09-26-setup-flow-in-core.message: Setup's Back button returns to the right step

2026-09-26-practice-workspace-in-core.message: The Getting Started practice starts from Crest's shared core

2026-09-26-typed-session-seeds.message: Crest hands its core typed sessions for new and test workspaces, and the core describes the first-launch session itself

2026-09-26-seeded-fixtures.message: Preview, showcase and test sessions are built as typed seeds the core opens

2026-09-26-password-files-in-core.message: Password file import and export run in Crest's shared core, which keeps none of the passwords it reads or writes

2026-09-26-native-core-test-target.message: The native core's test target builds with the support files its tests use

2026-09-26-review-build-tests-stay-unnam.message: Test runs hosted by review builds no longer open the review app's own session and stores

2026-09-26-webkit-downloads-through-core.message: WebKit's downloads run as the engine's own through the core, which asks where to save, whether to keep a risky file, and whether a site may download automatically

2026-09-26-seeded-sidebar-tests.message: Sidebar, split and window tests open typed seed sessions in the core

2026-09-26-engine-capabilities-follow-pa.message: Menus, the launcher and settings offer a feature when an engine Crest runs supports it, and the page's own engine decides whether it is available

2026-09-26-site-engine-choices.message: Crest can remember which engine each site's pages open on, per device, and keeps private windows' choices in memory only

2026-09-26-offer-default-and-live-engine.message: Features appear in menus and settings only for the default engine or an engine a page is open on

2026-09-26-sidebar-lift-speed.message: Picking up tabs, folders and multi-selections in the sidebar responds faster, especially with many tabs

2026-09-26-space-deletion-erases-every-e.message: Deleting a Space erases its website data in every browser engine Crest runs, including one that never opened a page for it

2026-09-26-engine-page-direct-path.message: Every engine answers a page's captures, exports, inspector, certificate and site decisions through one direct path

2026-09-26-shared-page-host.message: One page host keeps each window's pages on Mac, iPhone and iPad, and the core decides which pages memory pressure unloads on every device

2026-09-26-pages-move-engines-in-place.message: A page can move to another engine while keeping its tab, window and card

2026-09-26-rehost-pages-through-core.message: Pages can move to another engine through the core, keeping their tab and window

choose-site-engine.message: On Mac, Site Controls can open a site in WebKit or Chromium; the page moves there and the site keeps opening in that engine

protected-video-fallback.message: When a page's protected video needs a player Crest's Chromium doesn't have, the page moves to WebKit to play it, with an option to move it back

2026-09-26-chromium-reports-missing-drm.message: Chromium reports a missing Widevine or PlayReady to the core

2026-09-26-architecture-docs-current.message: The architecture documents describe the core, its contract and its engines as they are now

core-json-policy-boundary-removed.message: The core's last JSON policy entry point is gone; iPhone and iPad hand memory pressure to the core like the Mac.

core-engine-link-questions.message: The core decides where Chromium's links and self-opened pages go; context-menu rows are typed.

chromium-quick-window-popups.message: In the Chromium build, a pop-up opened from a Quick Window or Peek now opens in that window instead of disappearing.

2026-09-26-abi-check-unused-tag.message: The native ABI check sends a union tag far past every intent, so new intents never make it a real one

ios-residency-left-to-system.message: On iPhone and iPad, the system reclaims pages beyond the core's budget, as it does for Safari, and a reclaimed page reloads when shown.

credentials-read-spaces-from-read-model.message: Passwords and their prompts read Spaces from the core's read model

previews-draw-detached-read-model.message: Previews, setup drafts and import reviews draw Spaces the core resolves

staged-lift-expiry-manual-clock.message: Sidebar reorder expiry tests run on a clock the test moves

tab-rules-off-session-copy.message: Tab title and icon rules and native tabs read from the read model

extension-store-space-identities.message: Extensions and site controls name Spaces from the read model

delete-unused-swift-declarations.message: Unused Swift declarations removed after the core migration

remove-unused-catalog-strings.message: Unused localized strings removed from the catalog

delete-unread-policy-flags-dead-core-rul.message: Unread policy flags and unused core rules removed

chromium-menu-reads-offered-commands.message: The Chromium menu bar shows the commands the open pages' engines offer

chromium-private-window-borrowed-profile.message: Chromium private windows borrow only an unlocked Space's settings and extensions

page-hosts-read-read-model.message: Page hosts and engine glue read Spaces and tabs from the read model

shared-page-owner.message: iPhone, iPad and Mac page owners share one implementation of their common page work

chromium-private-window-starts-fresh.message: Chromium private windows start fresh each time, share nothing with any Space and run no extensions

chromium-engine-keeps-its-browsers.message: The Chromium engine keeps track of its own browser windows and tabs, and the Mac app only hosts their windows

session-copy-deleted.message: Swift keeps the browsing session only in the core's read model; its separate copy is gone

folder-symbol-stays-unset-across-sync.message: A folder without its own symbol keeps none when it syncs to another device

settings-bind-core-preferences.message: The Settings panes and page actions edit the core's own browsing, password and app preferences, with no Swift copy to convert them

settings-bind-core-branding.message: Space looks are drawn and edited as the core's own branding records, and the core works out each look's rendering vocabulary when it keeps it

webkit-binding-keeps-stores-and-rules.message: WebKit keeps each profile's website data and its pages' content rules itself, and private browsing drops its in-memory data when it ends

webkit-hands-core-restore-state-and-medi.message: WebKit hands the core the history of a page it unloads and reports each page's media as it changes, so memory pressure never asks pages first

page-host-follows-put-away-and-webkit-li.message: Closing a saved or pinned tab lets the page host put its page away after the core records it, and WebKit asks the core how each followed link opens and stages Peek links through it

settings-engine-pages-open-through-core.message: Chromium's feature flags page in Settings opens through the core like every other page, windows follow the session from the read model, and extension controls read their Space from it

synced-look-strength-once.message: A synced Space look keeps its banner strength; only a look from before the current rendering vocabulary is converted, once

native-views-and-preference-choices-desc.message: Settings and Getting Started tabs take their title and symbol from the core, and startup and saved-tab close choices carry their own titles

contract-records-share-concept-files.message: Contract records that only carry data share one file per concept, grouped in regions by message family and subject, instead of one file each

core-domain-data-types-grouped.message: The core's plain data types now sit beside the code that uses them instead of in files of their own.

swift-data-types-grouped.message: The apps' plain data types now sit beside the code that uses them or in one file per concept.

identities-named-by-uuid.message: Space, tab, folder, window, split and credential identities are plain UUIDs named by their role, with no aliases or wrapper types.

swift-sources-follow-formatter.message: Swift sources, including the Chromium app's, follow the project's formatting rules throughout.

extensions-live-with-their-owners.message: Extensions now live in files named for the type they extend, so each type's behaviour is found in one place.

platform-seams-stay-in-platform-layers.message: Shared browser code no longer depends on AppKit, UIKit or the logging framework directly; each platform supplies its own pieces, with no change in behaviour.

generated-password-records-redact-themse.message: Records that carry passwords to and from the core now describe themselves without naming any secret, generated from the core's contracts.

generated-message-handlers.message: The contract generator now gives each family of core messages a handler interface in the core and a handling protocol in the apps, so a new message without a handler fails to build.

core-receivers-use-message-handlers.message: Each part of the core now handles its messages through the generated handler interfaces instead of hand-written type switches, with no change in behaviour.

app-receivers-use-message-handlers.message: The apps' read model, engine bindings, pages and prompt followers now handle the core's changes, commands, requests and presentations through generated handling protocols, with no change in behaviour.

message-handling-documented.message: The architecture notes now describe how each receiver handles the core's messages through the generated handlers.

chromium-commands-dispatch-by-type.message: Chromium's engine handles each command the core sends through its own handler, so a new command can't be silently ignored.

generated-message-handlers-withdrawn.message: The core and the apps route their messages with the hand-written dispatch they used before the generated handlers, while each message family moves toward carrying its own behavior; nothing changes in behavior.

core-builds-as-one-assembly.message: The portable core now builds as one assembly, with its contracts, domain and application kept as folders and namespaces of it; nothing changes in behavior.

page-messages-carry-their-behavior.message: Each page intent and page event in the core now carries its own logic, so a new one that lacks it fails to build; nothing changes in behavior.

session-intents-carry-their-edits.message: Each session intent in the core now carries its own edit, so a new one that lacks it fails to build; nothing changes in behavior.

intents-route-themselves.message: Every intent now routes itself to the part of the core that owns it, and device, window, setup and workspace intents carry their own logic, so a new one that lacks either fails to build; nothing changes in behavior.

area-messages-carry-their-logic.message: Downloads, prompts, close preparations, data deletion, Space access and cloud sync intents, and the prompt and download events engines report, now carry their own logic, so a new one that lacks it fails to build; nothing changes in behavior.

queries-answer-themselves.message: Every question the core answers, and the one an engine asks while it waits, now carries its own answer, so a new one that lacks it fails to build; nothing changes in behavior.

swift-messages-carry-their-logic.message: In the apps, each change the core publishes, each command WebKit runs, each request its pages answer and each presentation Chromium shows now carries its own logic, so a new one that lacks it fails to build; nothing changes in behavior.

sync-removals-and-extension-commands.message: Each session change now names the synced records it removes, and the extension menu and settings ask the store with typed commands instead of words; nothing changes in behavior.

sync-record-names-from-their-kind.message: Every synced record's name is spelled by its record kind in one place.

dock-menu-spaces-and-window-commands.message: The Dock menu shows your Spaces and Crest's own window commands: New Window, New Quick Window and New Private Window.

space-icons-in-menus-every-time.message: Menus that list your Spaces show each Space's crest or symbol every time they open, including the link menu's Open Link in Another Space.

fullscreen-video-leaves-cleanly.message: Watching a video full screen no longer leaves a black screen that Esc and the window's buttons can't leave. The full-screen notice fades after a few seconds, and leaving full screen from the window's green button or the Window menu puts the page back in its place.

window-chrome-acts-as-title-bar.message: Dragging the sidebar background, the top of the window or the space around a page moves the window again, and double-clicking them does what System Settings says a title bar double-click does, while text near the top of a page can still be selected.

chromium-window-size-remembered.message: In the Chromium build, a new window opens at the size of the window you're using instead of its smallest size, and a window you close and reopen keeps saving its size.

sidebar-drop-into-open-lands-from-drop.message: A tab dragged into Open tabs now settles from where you drop it, instead of jumping back to where you picked it up first.

downloads-fly-to-the-box-on-every-engine.message: Starting a download in a Chromium window now shows the file flying from the pointer into the downloads box, which bounces as it lands, as it already did with WebKit.

extension-side-panel-follows-its-tab.message: An extension's side panel now follows the tab you're on. A panel an extension opened for one tab, such as Claude's, closes when you switch to another tab and comes back when you return, so it no longer answers about a tab you've left. A panel an extension shows for every tab stays open as you switch.

page-menu-rows-no-longer-quit.message: Choosing Open Link in Peek, Open Link in Split View, another Space or Search from a page's right-click menu works again instead of quitting Crest.

open-page-in-other-engine.message: In the Chromium build, the Page menu has Open Page in WebKit, so you can move a page to WebKit even before any page has opened there.

chromium-new-window-links-open-peek.message: In the Chromium build, a link that would open a new tab from a pinned or saved tab and leaves that tab's site opens in Peek, as it does in the WebKit build.

context-menu-row-test-keeps-its-page-vie.message: The context-menu row test keeps its page view alive, as the window does.

start-page-search-offers-commands.message: The Start Page's search now offers Crest's commands, like New Quick Window, when what you type matches one.

chromium-website-notifications-appear.message: In the Chromium build, notifications from sites you allow now appear as banners and in Notification Center, as they do in the WebKit build, and clicking one brings you to its tab. Private windows still show none.

now-playing-skips-notification-sounds-on.message: In the Chromium build, notification sounds and other short sounds a site plays no longer show the sidebar's Now Playing card or take over the Mac's Now Playing; only media you can play and pause does, as in the WebKit build.

chromium-build-names-itself-crest-to-mac.message: In the Chromium build, camera, microphone, location, Bluetooth and passkey prompts name Crest instead of Chromium, and Crest no longer includes a helper app that could appear as “Chromium” in Notifications settings.

picture-in-picture-returns-to-its-tab.message: The back-to-tab button in a Picture in Picture video now brings Crest forward on the video's own tab, switching window or Space if needed, in both the Chromium and WebKit builds. When you go back to that tab yourself, the video leaves Picture in Picture and returns to its place on the page, whether it floated automatically or you floated it.

webkit-tabs-show-engine-badge.message: In the Chromium build, tabs running in WebKit now show a small WebKit badge on their icon, so you can see at a glance which pages use WebKit.

page-top-keeps-its-drags.message: Dragging at the very top of a page, like selecting text or using YouTube's search box, no longer moves the window. The sidebar, the strip above the page and the space around it, and the top of a Quick Window, still move the window and do what your title bar double-click setting says.

opened-pages-keep-their-openers-engine.message: A sign-in window, a new tab or a Peek that a page opens now stays on that page's engine, so signing in with Google from a page moved to WebKit opens one sign-in page that finishes the sign-in, instead of several Chromium tabs.

popup-windows-open-in-quick-windows.message: Sign-in and other popup windows a page opens now appear in a Quick Window in the same Space, stay connected to the page that opened them, and close themselves when the sign-in finishes. Choose Open in to keep one as a tab.

locking-a-space-closes-its-picture-in-pi.message: Locking a protected Space, including when Crest goes to the background, now always closes that Space's Picture in Picture video.

webkit-badge-draws-stacked-tile.message: The WebKit badge on tab icons is clearer: it now shows a small blue-and-orange tile, which also appears beside WebKit in Site Controls' Opens in menu.

window-moves-natively-and-page-top-stays.message: Window › Move & Resize, the Globe-Control tiling shortcuts and the green button's tiling options work for Crest windows again, while dragging at the very top of a page still selects text instead of moving the window. Double-clicking empty sidebar space opens a new tab again, without also acting as a title bar double-click.

blank-popups-and-quick-window-popups-ope.message: A page that opens an empty window first and fills it in afterwards, as some sign-in buttons do, gets its window again instead of nothing. A link or script that opens a new window from a Quick Window or Peek loads in that window again, with Back and Forward, and a form posted that way keeps what it sent.

sign-in-popups-show-after-reopening-a-wi.message: Continue with Google and other sign-in popups open their Quick Window again in a window you closed and opened again, instead of doing nothing.

diagnostic-log-keeps-no-addresses.message: Crest's diagnostic log names a refused request by its rule alone, so it never keeps a site or an address, and the logging left over from earlier investigations is gone.

app-dead-code-after-restructure.message: The apps drop code the restructure left without callers: an unused download lookup, web-content load and reader toggle, a never-built device-validation trust path, two unused palette values, and two store logos nothing shows.

app-tests-trimmed-to-contracts.message: The app test suites drop tests that repeat a rule the core's own tests cover, re-test shared page code on iPhone, or check copy, and the test helpers nothing calls.

docs-describe-the-finished-design.message: The architecture and contributor documents describe the finished design, including popups in Quick Windows, the opener-engine rule, Picture in Picture, the title-bar guard and web notifications, instead of the restructure's plans and status.

third-party-notices-name-chromium-and-do.message: The third-party notices now include the bundled Chromium engine and .NET runtime, and the license audit checks them.

closed-window-stays-out-of-its-reopened-.message: A window you close while a Quick Window over it stays open no longer answers for the window that opens again in its place, so tabs and pop-ups a page opens show in the window you are using.

core-and-engine-dead-code-removed.message: Declarations nothing calls any more are gone from the core and the Chromium extension views.

core-test-leftovers-removed.message: The core's tests drop helpers left from the retired JSON protocol and a search test another one already covers.

core-contract-docs-describe-typed-querie.message: The contract README and the core's comments describe the typed queries and intents that replaced the JSON policy operations.

fixture-server-trust-query-removed.message: The core's fixture certificate trust query and the Chromium page's unused main-frame script call are gone, since nothing asks for them any more.

managed-chromium-fork-and-upstream-relea.message: Chromium builds use a managed workspace and a CI workflow with reviewed upstream updates and opt-in stable publication.

experimental-release-builds-missing-chro.message: Experimental releases build missing Chromium engines on the registered Mac and package one verified source revision. Automatic upstream publication is limited to experimental.

core-reports-arrive-whole.message: A page closed while it is still loading no longer leaves its old details behind, and updates from iCloud or a page always arrive in one piece.

core-published-lists-read-only.message: The session, sidebar and change lists the core accepts or publishes are read-only, so nothing that holds one can change the core's state behind its back.

folder-tree-indexed-lookups.message: Organizing tabs in a Space with many nested folders stays quick, because each folder edit looks folders up directly instead of searching them.

extension-background-window-keeps-focus.message: A window an extension opens in the background no longer takes keyboard focus from the window you are typing in.

closing-windows-asks-leaving-pages.message: Closing the private window, a window you tore a tab into, or a Quick Window now lets a page with unsaved work ask before it goes. Closing a regular window no longer asks, since its tabs stay open.

engine-hosted-page-typed.message: Shared page code names what an engine built for a page as its own type, and the WebKit pieces it carried now live with the WebKit engine.

chromium-first-run-setup.message: The Chromium build now opens first-run setup on a Mac where Crest hasn't been set up yet, as the WebKit build does, and opens your windows once setup finishes.

quit-waits-for-space-deletion.message: Quitting while a Space is being deleted now tells you Crest will quit once the Space is gone, and then quits by itself, instead of quitting midway or ignoring the request.

external-opens-follow-link-settings.message: Links and documents from other apps open in your frontmost Crest window, and with no window open they follow your link settings instead of always opening a Quick Window. The Chromium build reopens its windows in the order you left them, with only the front one taking focus.

one-mac-shell-for-both-engines.message: Both Mac builds share one AppKit shell for their windows, menu bar, launch, reopen, outside opens and quit, and the Chromium build now runs on it; its windows tell their content when they are minimized or hidden.

dock-icon-download-progress.message: Crest's Dock icon shows how many downloads are in progress and how far along they are, and keeps the app icon you picked while it does.

webkit-build-on-shared-mac-shell.message: The WebKit build now runs on the same Mac app shell as the Chromium build, so both reopen the windows you left open in the order you left them, and both put links from other apps where your link settings say even with no window open. The first launch after this update reopens your most recently used window at its default size.

edit-menu-text-tools-in-both-builds.message: The Chromium build's Edit menu now has Find, Spelling and Grammar, Substitutions, Transformations and Speech, Translate Page appears in the Page menu whenever a page can be translated, and Command-W closes Crest Setup and What's New in Crest there too.

extension-closed-tabs-close-once.message: A tab or window an extension closes now closes in Crest instead of leaving a blank tab behind, and a site can close only a tab or window that another page opened.

dock-keeps-picked-icon-during-downloads.message: The Dock keeps the app icon you picked while downloads run.

extension-windows-close-themselves.message: Windows and tabs an extension opens, such as a password manager's pop-out, can close themselves again when they're done.

iphone-new-tab-search-shows-page.message: A search from a new tab on iPhone shows its page right away instead of a blank screen.

setup-no-longer-waits-on-icloud.message: Setup no longer waits forever when iCloud doesn't answer: after a few seconds you can set up without it, and sync tries iCloud again on its own.

core-lays-out-command-menus.message: The core lays out the menu bar's command menus and the launcher's command list, which the Mac shell builds from, so every command keeps a menu item and a shortcut.

quick-window-closes-with-its-page.message: A Quick Window whose page closes itself, such as a sign-in window once you're signed in, now closes even while it's asking whether you want to leave the page.

sign-in-popup-test-waits-for-its-page.message: The sign-in popup test waits for the consent page to finish loading before it clicks.

fullscreen-video-no-longer-black.message: Videos you play full screen, such as on YouTube, show again instead of a black screen.

fullscreen-standard-title-bar.message: In full screen, the title bar that slides down with the menu bar looks like the standard one instead of a blank block over the page.

pages-get-first-say-over-shortcuts.message: Pages get first say over shortcuts such as ⌘F, as in other browsers, so a document editor like Google Docs opens its own Find. ⌘T, ⌘W and ⌘N always stay Crest's.

now-playing-artwork-on-chromium.message: Now Playing shows the track's artwork again for pages that run in Chromium, including artwork from sites you're signed in to, sized to fit music and video.

chromium-runner-builds-inside-its-worksp.message: The Chromium engine builder accepts the checkout its own Actions runner makes inside the build workspace.

mouse-back-forward-once-per-click.message: A mouse's Back and Forward buttons move one page per click on pages that run in Chromium, instead of two.

mouse-back-forward-one-page-every-click.message: A mouse's Back and Forward buttons move one page per click, every time, including on pages that run in Chromium.

swipe-back-forward-on-chromium-pages.message: Swiping back and forward works on pages that run in Chromium, including a mouse's Back and Forward actions set up in Logitech Options+ and three-finger swipes between pages.

pointer-hides-over-fullscreen-video.message: The pointer hides over a video playing full screen in a window that was already full screen, and pages that change the pointer no longer wait for the mouse to move.

fullscreen-title-bar-leaves-no-bar.message: In full screen, the title bar that slides down with the menu bar goes away with it instead of leaving a white or black bar across the top of the window or video.

fullscreen-video-in-fullscreen-window.message: With Crest already in full screen, a full-screen video covers the whole screen, and Esc brings the sidebar back while Crest stays in full screen.

screen-sharing-site-setting.message: Site settings have a Screen Sharing choice, so you can block a site from asking to share your screen; macOS still asks what to share every time.

chromium-screen-sharing-system-picker.message: Screen sharing on pages that run in Chromium uses the macOS sharing picker and needs no Screen Recording permission, and Crest no longer asks for that permission over and over.

media-pages-stay-loaded.message: A tab that plays sound or video, has a video in Picture in Picture, even paused, or uses your camera or microphone stays open and loaded however long you are away from it.

page-presentation-diagnostics.message: Crest's Pages log records which pages each window shows, when Chromium is told to show or hide one, Picture in Picture, memory pressure and a page's first input after it returns.

space-return-shows-pages.message: Pages in a Space you leave rest like background tabs, and coming back shows them, split views included, the way switching to their tab does, without taking focus from the address field or the command palette.

chromium-media-pages-never-frozen.message: Chromium never freezes a background tab that plays sound or video, has a video in Picture in Picture, even paused, or uses your camera, microphone or screen.

engine-default-and-website-rules.message: Choose your default browsing engine and add, edit or remove website engine rules in Settings. Chromium is recommended, while WebKit offers native handling and FairPlay video.

chromium-loads-when-needed.message: WebKit sessions leave Chromium unloaded until you open a Chromium website or extension. Once loaded, it stays ready until you quit Crest.

dual-engine-default-desktop-download.message: The default Mac download includes Chromium and WebKit, with a separate WebKit build available. Each build keeps its own update channel.

session-snapshots-own-nested-values.message: Published session snapshots own their nested collections, including record copies, so callers cannot mutate accepted browsing state.

chromium-extension-window-geometry.message: Extensions can move, resize and restore Crest windows using their normal window controls.

cloud-convergence-typed-session.message: Cloud convergence materializes and repairs typed sessions while keeping local credentials, page assets and pending profile deletion work on the receiving device.

experimental-updates-continue-on-develop.message: The final experimental update moves your update preference to Development so future Crest updates continue there.

engine-settings-localization-catalog.message: Refresh generated localization metadata for engine settings while preserving existing translations.

chromium-space-swipe-keeps-pages-renderi.message: Chromium pages keep rendering while you swipe between Spaces instead of turning gray.

find-return-steps-one-match.message: Pressing Return in Find moves to the next match instead of skipping several ahead.

single-mac-download.message: Crest for Mac is one download with both engines. Copies of the separate WebKit download update to it automatically.

split-click-focuses-field.message: Clicking a field in the other half of a split view lets you type there on the first click.

extension-popup-close-no-crash.message: Crest no longer quits when an extension closes its popup window, as Bitwarden does after you turn on unlock with biometrics.

extension-popups-open-as-tabs.message: Extension popups, such as a password manager's settings popout, open as a tab in your current window instead of a new window.

updates-install-after-restart.message: Restarting to install an update, or choosing Quit from the Dock, quits Crest so the update installs instead of waiting forever.

floating-sidebar-stays-for-its-popups.message: A hidden sidebar you've revealed stays open while something you opened from it is still on screen, like an extension popup, a folder color picker, or a confirmation, and while you're renaming something in it.

folder-symbol-follows-tinted-title.message: Folder symbols take the folder color when tinted folder titles are turned on.

feature-flags-follow-webkit-default.message: Feature Flags in Settings shows WebKit's flags when WebKit is your default engine, instead of an empty page.

command-palette-animation-setting.message: You can turn off the animation from the address field into the command palette in Look and Feel, so the palette opens right away.

web-store-button-every-language.message: Add to Crest works on Chrome Web Store pages in every language, including an extension's reviews and support pages, and the store's prompts to switch to Chrome stay hidden.

collapsed-folder-keeps-nested-tab.message: Collapsing a folder keeps the tab you're on visible even when it sits in a folder inside it, shown under each folder that holds it.

nested-folder-from-kept-path-opens-paren.message: Making a nested folder from a folder shown on a collapsed folder's way to its kept tab opens the folders around it, so the new folder appears ready to name.

chromium-fullscreen-video-hides-idle-poi.message: Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit.

space-page-takes-input-after-late-switch.message: A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs.

hidden-sidebar-reveals-only-in-front-win.message: A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open.

drag-window-by-page-frame.message: Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.

developer-toolbar-local-pages-setting.message: A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.

chromium-screen-sharing-without-click.message: Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share.

tab-titles-follow-late-page-titles.message: Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder.

chromium-untitled-pages-keep-titles.message: Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.

chromium-host-patch-applies-to-fresh-sou.message: Crest's Chromium changes apply cleanly to freshly prepared engine sources, so upstream Chromium updates can build.

downloads-follow-page-site-choice.message: Downloads follow the Automatic Downloads choice of the site you’re on, including files it serves from another address, such as GitHub release files. A blocked download’s message no longer appears twice.

chromium-pages-retain-requested-zoom.message: Chromium pages use your default zoom when they open and keep your chosen zoom as you navigate.

chromium-upstream-154-0-8037-57-1-1-1c2d.message: Chromium is updated to 154.0.8037.57 with upstream security and compatibility fixes.

protected-video-consented-engine-switch.message: Protected-video pages still switch to WebKit automatically. Engine switches respect unsaved-changes prompts and remember the website only after the move is allowed.

chromium-profile-adoption-recovery.message: Interrupted Chromium profile upgrades resume safely without losing track of your existing browsing profiles.

chromium-download-pause-and-recovery.message: Pause and resume Chromium downloads, and recover interrupted transfers when the server supports it.

chromium-local-background-notifications.message: Chromium can show local service-worker and extension notifications while Crest runs, with Space access and notification permissions respected.

release-source-validation-and-startup-co.message: Validate the exact source before release, build the current native core with the Chromium host, and make startup cancellation and deferred requests explicit.

chromium-update-macos-requirement.message: Crest updates advertise the macOS version the whole app requires, so older Macs are not offered an incompatible update.

crest-07-chromium-and-webkit.message: Crest 0.7 brings Chromium and WebKit together on Mac, with Chrome Web Store extensions and engine choices for each website. iPhone and iPad continue to use WebKit.

opaque-mac-windows-external-display-load.message: Crest windows on Mac no longer keep the system's WindowServer busy, which could use a lot of CPU on large or high-refresh external displays. The focused-window transparency setting has been removed.

window-focus-bridge-release-format.message: Format the browser window's focus bridge to the release lint rules.

tab-switch-cpu-and-energy.message: Switching tabs on Mac uses a fraction of the CPU and energy it did. The window no longer redraws or animates everything on each switch, and tab use and page visits now sync in batches in the background.

tab-switch-without-blank-frames.message: Switching tabs on Mac no longer flashes a blank page in between, and a tab loading for the first time keeps a plain page background instead of flashing the Space's colors.

web-store-large-extensions.message: Large Chrome Web Store extensions such as Keeper now install on Mac. Extensions download through the Space's own connection, as they do in Chrome, and the install review shows download progress.

web-store-download-cancel.message: Stop an extension package download when its install review closes.

login-button-federated-sign-in-crash.message: Crest on Mac no longer quits when you press a site’s Login or Continue with Google button. Crest doesn’t offer Chrome’s federated sign-in, so these sites use their own sign-in pop-up or page where they have one, as they do in Safari.

extension-sign-in-survives-relaunch.message: Extensions that sign you back in on their own when the browser starts, such as Claude, now stay signed in after Crest restarts on Mac, as they do in Chrome.

extension-tab-groups-as-folders.message: Tab groups that extensions make, such as the tabs Claude works in, now appear on Mac as folders in the Space’s open tabs, in the group’s name and color. Renaming, recoloring, collapsing or deleting the folder, or moving tabs in or out, changes the group the extension sees, and the folder keeps following the group after Crest restarts.

retina-tab-icons.message: Site icons in tabs and pinned tabs on Mac are now sharp on Retina displays instead of blurry.

back-forward-history-menu-responsive.message: The back and forward history menus open at once and no longer freeze Crest on Mac when you move the pointer over them. Each lists the 12 nearest pages, with Show Full History at the end for everything else.

zen-import-pinned-split-views.message: Importing from Zen no longer fails with “Crest could not recognize this browser’s tab-session data” when a Space has pinned tabs in a split view. Those tabs now come over as saved tabs: in the folder that held the split, or outside any folder when the split sat among the Space’s pinned tabs. A Zen session too large to import now says so.

site-controls-full-screen.message: Site Controls and the extensions it lists now open on Mac when the window is in full screen, instead of closing as soon as you click the button.

extension-download-startup-hold.message: Installing an extension right after Crest opens no longer stays on “Preparing extension…” for up to three minutes.

import-chrome-arc-extensions.message: Importing from Chrome, Arc, or another Chromium browser now lists the extensions you installed from the Chrome Web Store beneath each Space’s address bar. Choose which ones each Space brings, and Crest installs them when the import finishes, without asking about each one.

import-more-chromium-browsers.message: You can now import from Brave, Microsoft Edge, Vivaldi, Opera, Dia, Comet, Aside, ego lite, Chromium, and Chrome Beta, Dev, and Canary. If your browser isn’t listed, choose “Browser not listed?” to have Crest look for other Chromium-based browsers on your Mac.

import-split-views-and-tab-groups.message: Importing now keeps split views from Chrome and other Chromium browsers, Arc, and Zen, and turns tab groups from Chromium browsers and Firefox into folders with the same names and colors.

import-chrome-closed-profile-tabs.message: Importing from Chrome no longer leaves out a profile, or brings its recently closed tabs instead of the ones it had open.

import-passwords-stay-with-their-profile.message: Passwords imported from a browser profile now go only to that profile’s Space, so turning off passwords for one profile no longer sends them to another. Arc passwords also reach Spaces whose tabs are on a subdomain of the password’s site.

import-keeps-what-fits.message: When an import holds more than Crest can keep, it now brings as many Spaces, tabs, folders, and bookmarks as fit and lists what it left out, instead of stopping. A Space that joins one of yours brings only the tabs it has room for.

import-signed-in-chrome-bookmarks.message: Importing a Chrome profile signed in to a Google account now brings the bookmarks and passwords saved to that account, and bookmarks in a browser’s trash are no longer imported.

import-zen-firefox-profiles.message: Importing from Zen or Firefox now brings every profile that has open tabs, each under the name you gave it, and Zen Spaces keep their icons and colors.

import-safari-pinned-tabs.message: Importing from Safari now brings your pinned tabs, and its bookmark folders keep the names Safari shows, such as Favorites and Reading List.

import-open-tabs-stay-open.message: Tabs that were open in the browser you import from now stay open instead of being archived by automatic cleanup soon after the import, and Arc tabs keep their real dates.

import-review-design.message: The import review has matching From and Into menus and one card for each Space’s choices, and says when there’s no room for another Space. The list of browsers scrolls when it doesn’t fit the window.

settings-native-redesign.message: Settings has a cleaner, native look with less text. Each Space has its own page in the Settings sidebar, where you can add, rename, rearrange, lock and delete Spaces, and tab options have their own Tabs page.

crest-studio-forge.message: Crest Studio shows your crest on your Space’s own background, names every color by what it paints, and walks you through shape, field, band, emblem, border, finish and sidebar with previews of your crest. Each part of a crest can now have its own color.

settings-space-switch-speed.message: Switching Spaces with Settings open is now as quick as with a webpage, and Settings pages scroll smoothly.

crest-template-arms.message: Every Space template has new arms in colors of their own, from a grey wolf on snow to a pale raven on black, and Shuffle now changes every part of a crest and its sidebar.

declared-fixed-set-facts.message: Crest's fixed sets declare their own facts, such as a crest term's rendering vocabulary, ranges and titles, instead of working them out in switches across the apps and the core.

stored-address-loads.message: Tabs with very long addresses, or addresses that aren’t ordinary web links, open where they were instead of turning into a search.

ipad-single-tap-controls.message: On iPad, buttons and menus such as Manage Search Engines respond to a single tap or click instead of needing a long press.

sidebar-hover-area-width.message: Choose how wide the edge of the window is that shows a hidden sidebar, in Appearance settings. The edge lights up while you adjust it.

full-screen-sidebar-flicker.message: The strip along the top of a full-screen window no longer flickers when the sidebar opens.

mobile-launch-crash.message: Crest on iPhone and iPad opens again instead of closing as soon as it starts.

camera-microphone-allow-crash.message: Allowing a site to use your camera or microphone no longer quits Crest.

onboarding-scan-for-more.message: Setup no longer looks through other browsers’ data when Crest first opens. It reads a browser only when you choose it to import, or everything when you press Scan for more.

pinned-tab-unpin-menu.message: A pinned tab's menu now offers Unpin Tab, and a selection of pinned tabs offers Unpin Tabs.

concentric-page-corners.message: On Mac, a page’s corners now follow the rounded corners of its window, so the window border stays the same width all the way around at any border size.

full-screen-page-top-band.message: On Mac, pages no longer show a dark band across their tops after the window enters full screen.

update-restart-recovers.message: Restarting to install an update no longer gets stuck. If you choose to stay on a page, the update goes back to Ready to Install so you can restart when you’re ready, and a page asking before you leave now comes to the front.

update-card-hide.message: You can hide the update card in the sidebar until you next check for updates or restart Crest. Settings › About shows where the update stands and offers the same buttons.

show-history-opens-sidebar.message: On Mac, Show History now opens a hidden sidebar, as Show Archive and Show Downloads do. The History, Archive and Downloads button now sits on the page side of the sidebar, whichever side the sidebar is on, so its shortcuts open beside the sidebar instead of over it, in right-to-left languages too.

chromium-tab-history-after-relaunch.message: On Mac, tabs that use Chromium keep their back and forward history when you quit and reopen Crest, as WebKit tabs already did.

no-chromium-folder-on-quit.message: On Mac, quitting Crest no longer creates an empty Chromium folder in Application Support, where another Chromium browser keeps its profile.

reopened-windows-after-quit.message: On Mac, Crest reopens the windows that were open when you quit, instead of sometimes bringing back windows you had already closed.

chromium-tab-history-across-updates.message: On Mac, tabs that use Chromium keep their back and forward history when Crest or macOS updates.

chromium-upstream-154-0-8037-97-1-1-6c05.message: Chromium is updated to 154.0.8037.97 with upstream security and compatibility fixes.

screen-sharing-tab-picker.message: Sharing your screen on a page that runs in Chromium now lets you share a single tab, with its sound, as well as a window or your whole screen.

icloud-sync-tabs-moved-between-spaces.message: iCloud sync no longer stops on your other devices after you move a tab to another Space. A device that stopped picks up again once all your devices are on this version.

sync-buttons-on-their-own-rows.message: On iPhone and iPad, Sync Now and Pull from iCloud each have their own row in Sync settings, so each one responds to a tap.

icloud-sync-catches-up-on-open.message: iCloud sync catches up each time Crest opens. Changes made on your other devices while Crest was closed arrive, and changes waiting on this device upload, without tapping Sync Now.

icloud-sync-status-shows-waiting-uploads.message: Sync settings say Up to date only when every change has reached iCloud, and Waiting to upload while some haven’t yet.

command-palette-ranks-and-searches-sites.message: The command palette puts the best match first, ranks the pages and tabs you use most and most recently, and learns which result you choose for what you type. It fills in sites you visit, including those that start with www, and Return opens what it filled in. Before you type it lists your recent tabs, so Return takes you back to the one you were on. Start typing a provider’s name or shortcut, such as yt for YouTube or claude, to see it under the field, and press Tab to search that site or ask that assistant directly. Hold Command, Shift or Option with Return to open a result in the background, in Split View or in a Quick Window. The new Search section in Settings sets one default search for every Space and one for private windows, turns search engines, AI assistants and websites on or off with options of their own, such as hiding Google’s AI Overviews, adds your own, and chooses what the palette shows, how many of each, and in what order.

search-logos-keep-proportions.message: Search engine and assistant logos in Settings keep their proportions instead of looking stretched.

space-switching-keeps-crest-open.message: Switching Spaces no longer makes Crest quit unexpectedly on macOS 26.

settings-opens-in-browser-window.message: Settings opens in your browser window instead of a new window while a Quick Window is in front.

start-on-new-tab.message: On iPhone and iPad, Start on new tab in General settings opens Crest on a new tab in your default Space, ready to search.

floating-sidebar-optional.message: On iPhone the sidebar stays full screen. Turn on Allow floating sidebar in General settings to float it over the page instead.

floating-sidebar-buttons-respond.message: Buttons in the floating sidebar respond to taps, and its Settings button opens Settings.

settings-shows-real-app-icon.message: Settings on iPhone and iPad shows Crest’s real app icon, including the one you chose, in light and dark.

default-browser-status-remembered.message: On iPhone and iPad, General settings shows whether Crest is your default browser instead of Unavailable when iOS limits how often Crest can check.

search-provider-editor-opens.message: Edit Shortcuts and Add Provider in Search settings open right away on iPhone and iPad.

space-search-picker-icons.message: A Space’s Search with menu shows each provider’s icon, like the default search menu.

settings-section-colors.message: Each section in Settings has its own color, drawn from the Space templates.

history-opens-over-page.message: On iPhone, Show Full History in a page’s Back and Forward menus opens History.

download-prompt-over-page.message: On iPhone, Crest asks before downloading a risky file from the page you’re viewing, instead of leaving the download waiting for approval.

tab-audio-indicator.message: A tab playing sound shows a speaker badge on its icon, which mutes or unmutes it, and bars behind its title that follow its sound on Chromium pages. Tabs taking part in tab sharing show a badge that goes to the other tab or stops sharing. Look and Feel can show the status in place of the tab’s icon, or turn the bars off.

page-commands-follow-peek.message: While a Peek is open, Copy Link, Share, Find, Zoom, Reload, Back, Forward, Print, Export as PDF and Save Web Archive act on the page in the Peek instead of the tab behind it, and Close Tab closes the Peek.

find-next-shortcut.message: Command-G and Command-Shift-G move to the next and previous find-in-page match, and reopen the find bar with your last search.

agents-use-crest.message: On Mac, coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex can use Crest as their browser in the Spaces you choose: open and read tabs, click and type, take screenshots, and read a page’s console and network requests. Turn it on in Settings › Agents. Crest asks before each new agent connects, and every tab an agent uses shows its badge.
